**3B.8 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024**

**Working judgment:** `Mixed / partial` because there is evidence of tolerated protest and some democratic space, but also consistent red-tagging, surveillance pressure, and selective intimidation around dissent.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Positive | PBBM declares free, safe environment for journalists under Bagong Pilipinas | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-15 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-declares-free-safe-environment-for-journalists-under-bagong-pilipinas/ | Marcos publicly pledged press freedom and journalist safety. This is direct pro-dissent rhetoric, though it is official intent rather than proof of practice. | 3B.8, 3B.3 |
| Positive | Gov’t vows legal action vs deep fake video creators, spreaders | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-26 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/govt-vows-legal-action-vs-deep-fake-video-creators-spreaders/ | The government responded to a manipulated deepfake video with investigation and legal action rather than broader repression. This is evidence of a non-punitive response to information disorder. | 3B.8, 3B.6 |
| Positive | PCO to designate fact-check officers in state media to fight fake news | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-09-09 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pco-to-designate-fact-check-officers-in-state-media-to-fight-fake-news/ | PCO said it would add fact-check officers in state media and denied a policy or practice of red-tagging. This is modest evidence of an attempt to reduce informational repression. | 3B.8, 3B.6, 3B.3 |
| Positive | PBBM says Philippines not in business of instigating wars | Reuters / ThePrint | 2024-06-23 | https://theprint.in/world/philippines-not-in-business-of-instigating-wars-says-president-marcos/2143467/ | Marcos said the state would settle disputes peacefully and not use force or intimidation. This supports a broader tolerance for nonviolent dissent and public contestation rather than coercion. | 3B.8, 2B.6, 2B.7 |
| Positive | The government expanded public access through the eFOI portal and kept a media-literacy / disinformation campaign in place | Philippine News Agency | 2024-01-18 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217036 | Expanded eFOI access and a standing media-literacy/disinformation campaign support a lower-chilling-effect public sphere. This is indirect but relevant to free association and protest. | 3B.8, 3B.6 |
| Negative | Philippines | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines | The report says red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats against journalists persisted under Marcos. This indicates ongoing chilling pressure on dissent, even if not always direct retaliation. | 3B.8, 3B.3, 3B.6 |
| Negative | Philippines: “I turned my fear into courage”: Red-tagging and state violence against young human rights defenders in the Philippines | Amnesty International | 2024-10-14 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa35/8574/2024/en/ | Amnesty says Marcos-era actors used misinformation and anti-terror framing to create fear, and red-tagging vilified activists, journalists, teachers, and others as extremists. This is strong evidence of a hostile climate for dissent. | 3B.8, 3B.6, 3B.3 |
| Negative | Philippines: Dangerous “Red Tagging” of Labor Leaders | Human Rights Watch | 2024-09-25 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders | HRW reports officials and police or military members threatened union leaders by accusing them of communist links. That is clear intimidation of community organization and labor dissent. | 3B.8, 3B.2, 3B.3 |
| Negative | Philippines: “Red-Tagging” Puts Activists at Risk | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/philippines-red-tagging-puts-activists-risk | HRW says red-tagging under Marcos placed leftist activists and critics at serious risk and was used by officials/supporters to accuse them of insurgent ties. This is direct evidence against a clean tolerance of dissent. | 3B.8, 3B.3, 3B.2 |
| Negative | World Report 2024: Philippines | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/philippines | HRW says government officials and supporters continued red-tagging activists, unionists, Indigenous leaders, teachers, students, and journalists. This undercuts claims of broad freedom from selective punishment. | 3B.8, 3B.3, 3B.2 |

**Synthesis**
- There is some real positive evidence: Marcos’s public rhetoric, the deepfake response, fact-checking steps, and broader information-access tools.
- But the negative evidence is substantial and more specific: red-tagging, threats, blocked sites, and intimidation of activists and union leaders persisted through 2024.
- Best read: `some space for protest and speech, but not free of chilling pressure or selective punishment`.

**Search gap**
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence of Marcos personally ordering crackdowns on ordinary protest movements.
- The main pattern is tolerated or enabled intimidation by officials, security actors, and supporters, rather than a clearly documented blanket ban on dissent.
